metadata.name: Bonapartism
metadata.description: The early Napoleonic tradition of central executive authority, plebiscitary legitimacy, civil equality and protected property. This profile covers its First Empire foundations, rather than every later Bonapartist movement.
metadata.scope: The political principles of the early Napoleonic settlement: executive and dynastic authority claiming national delegation, uniform civil law, property rights, state administration and national power. Bonapartism developed as a named movement after 1815; later liberal-imperial and social programmes are not projected backwards.
metadata.phrase: A society united by a strong national executive, supported through public ratification, that maintains civil equality, secure property and an orderly state.
